evolve: Use when code should run faster or score higher and something already measures it (a benchmark, a test suite, a metric, a target number), and the user wants the best version, not the first that works; or when the user names AlphaEvolve, FunSearch or autoresearch. Runs a propose → score → improve loop and checks the winner on held-out data; about 15 minutes (5 if asked to be quick, no limit if told to take its time). Not when nothing can score the result, any correct answer will do, or the code is slow and nothing measures it yet (that is profile-first).
profile-first: Use when code is slow and nothing measures it yet: the user asks why it is slow, what takes the time, or to make it faster or cut its run time, latency or startup. Measures before anything is sped up: profiles a production-sized input in fresh processes, splits out import time and I/O wait, and confirms each hot spot by timing the whole run without it. Python commands that run to completion; whole-run timing for any command; macOS and Linux. Pasted code that cannot run here: names no hot spot and says what to measure. Not when a benchmark or score already measures the code (that is evolve), or the change is already specified.
